title: Sketch map assessment criteria
subject: Geography
unit: Spring 2: Map skills and fieldwork (Tribal Tales)
source: Written for geography/y3 lesson 14 (Sketch map assessment criteria (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 14: Fieldwork at home: my sketch map. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Our fieldwork guide
points: Stay indoors: look from a window
Or map your room or garden with an adult

model.title: Sketch map of a street from a window

parts.text: Draw the road across the page
Add a tree symbol and a lamp post
Add a key and north arrow

panels.title: Compare with a real map
points: Open satellite view with an adult

keywords.def: finding out by looking and recording in a real place
a quick map drawn from what we see
a map of a small place from above
an arrow that shows which way is north
say what is the same and different

questions.q: What three things must every map have?
questions.a: A key, a north arrow and a title (labels too)

questions.q: Core: Draw your sketch map (room, garden or window view) with a title, key and north arrow.
questions.a: A sketch map with title, key and north arrow (assessed against the map criteria)

questions.q: Extend: Write two ways your map differs from the satellite image.
questions.a: For example: I missed the shed; my road was too wide

questions.q: Stretch: Add a four-figure grid and give one grid reference.
questions.a: A grid and a correct reference
A) From above. Maps show places from above.
Finding out by looking in a real place
options: Finding out by looking in a real place

questions.q: Big question: can you map a place without another map?
questions.a: Yes, with careful looking, a key and a north arrow, though it may not be exact
